bugs: Completion is tracked with plain counters (processed_accounts/failed_accounts increments, app/Models/StatementRun.php:36-43), so it is not idempotent. SQS delivers at least once, so a redelivered or retried GenerateStatement increments processed_accounts again. Probe: running the same job twice with total_accounts=2 marked the run Completed while one account was never processed, and sent StatementReady twice.

If handle() succeeds and then something later throws (for example the summary mail inside recordAttempt), the retry or failed() counts the account again. Probe: handle() followed by failed() left processed=2 and failed=1 for a single account, so failed_accounts can be wrong.

DispatchStatementChunk has Tries(3) and increments dispatched_accounts before Queue::bulk (app/Jobs/DispatchStatementChunk.php:41-46). If a chunk fails partway and is retried, dispatched_accounts and so total_accounts are overcounted, and the run never reaches the total.

total_accounts is first set from the active count when the action runs, and settleTotal only fixes it after the last chunk. An account activated in between (id <= maxId) can make the run complete early while jobs are still pending.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:27 ShouldBeUnique/UniqueFor does nothing: Queue::bulk calls the queue's push directly and skips PendingDispatch, which is where the unique lock is taken. It is ceremony that suggests dedup protection the code does not have.

app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:70-72 and app/Jobs/DispatchStatementChunk.php:56-58 repeat the summary-mail dispatch. It belongs in one place, for example inside finishIfAllAttempted or a model method.
app/Models/StatementRun.php:11-21 the extra dispatched/processed counter columns plus the $attributes defaults add bookkeeping that the migration defaults already cover.
database/factories/StatementRunFactory.php:18 a random total_accounts in the factory default makes tests less deterministic.
app/Jobs/GenerateStatement.php:35 sets the queue with onQueue in the constructor plus a QUEUE constant, where the #[Queue] attribute would do.
strengths: Chunked, self-chaining fan-out (1000 ids per job) using Queue::bulk, which SqsQueue sends as SendMessageBatch. This scales to 40k accounts without one long-running dispatcher job.
Accounts are passed as ids and re-fetched with active() inside the job, so deleted or deactivated accounts are counted as processed and the run still finishes (verified by probe).
Atomic claim of the Running to final transition with a conditional UPDATE, so only one worker sends the summary.
Skips regeneration when the PDF already exists on retry; slow work runs on the 'statements' queue with Timeout/Tries/Backoff attributes.

Tests run a real queue worker (database driver plus travel) so retries and failed() are exercised end to end, and they cover chunk splitting, deactivation mid-run and the empty run. Markdown mail views are idiomatic.

bugs: GenerateAccountStatement serialises the BillingAccount model and has #[DeleteWhenMissingModels] (app/Jobs/GenerateAccountStatement.php:24,29). If an account is deleted between dispatch and processing, the job is dropped silently without a result row or failed(), so the run stays 'running' forever and the summary is never sent. Verified by probe: status Running, total 2.

DispatchStatementJobs pushes all ~40k jobs one at a time (GenerateAccountStatement::dispatch in a lazyById loop, app/Jobs/DispatchStatementJobs.php:27-29). It runs as a single job on the default queue with no #[Timeout] and #[Tries(1)]. On SQS, 40k sequential SendMessage calls will very likely exceed the default 60s worker timeout. The job is then killed and marked failed with no retry, total_accounts is never settled, part of the fan-out is missing, and the run never completes.

total_accounts starts as the active count when the action runs and is only corrected after dispatching finishes. An account activated in between (id <= maxAccountId) can let completeIfFinished finish the run early while one job is still pending.
completeIfFinished runs two COUNT queries over the ledger after every job (O(n) each, about 40k times per run). It is acceptable but wasteful compared with atomic counters.
antipatterns: database/migrations/2026_11_07_000002_create_statement_runs_table.php:21-29 statement_run_accounts gains about 40k rows per run (roughly 480k a year) with no pruning (no MassPrunable), which conflicts with the 'tables do not grow forever' goal.
app/Jobs/DispatchStatementJobs.php:28 per-item dispatch instead of Queue::bulk or chunked fan-out for 40k jobs.
app/Actions/StartStatementRun.php:16 passes failed_accounts => 0 explicitly when the column already defaults to 0.
app/Models/StatementRun.php:64 sends mail from inside an Eloquent model method, which mixes side effects into the model.
strengths: Idempotent per-account ledger with a unique (run, account) index and insertOrIgnore, so duplicate SQS deliveries do not inflate counts, and failed_accounts is derived from the ledger and accurate (verified by probe).
Generator exceptions are caught and reported, so one bad account is recorded as failed immediately without burning retries. failed() covers other exhausted failures such as mail.
Atomic conditional-UPDATE claim, so the summary is sent exactly once; snapshotting maxAccountId keeps accounts created later out of the run.
Modern attributes throughout (#[Queue], #[Tries], #[Backoff], #[Timeout], #[Scope], #[Fillable]); StatementReady attaches the PDF via Attachment::fromStorageDisk.
Tests are concise, fast Pest tests covering the failure path, double execution, the failed() hook, the empty run and mailable rendering.

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-1 first. Both test suites pass (impl-2: 10 tests; impl-1: 11 tests). Both use the same overall design: a dispatcher job on the default queue, per-account jobs on the 'statements' queue, and an atomic conditional-UPDATE claim of the final status.

**Impl-2.** Its idempotent per-account results table keeps failed_accounts accurate even when SQS delivers a job twice. But it breaks the requirement that the run always reaches a final status in two ways:
- **Deleted account:** the job has #[DeleteWhenMissingModels] on a serialised account. If the account is deleted mid-run, the job is dropped silently and the run stays 'running' forever. A probe confirmed this.
- **The 40k fan-out:** a single dispatcher job sends about 40k individual SQS messages, with Tries(1) and no timeout. It will very likely be killed by the worker timeout, leaving the run stuck and partly dispatched.

Impl-2 also adds a results table that grows by about 40k rows every month with no pruning.

**Impl-1.** It handles the scale requirement properly: chunked, self-chaining fan-out that sends batches through Queue::bulk (SQS SendMessageBatch). It re-fetches accounts by id, so deleted or deactivated accounts still count and the run finishes (also confirmed by probe). Its weakness is counter-based tracking. Under duplicate delivery or a retry after partial success, counts go up again: a probe showed a premature 'completed' and a duplicate owner email. Its ShouldBeUnique does nothing because Queue::bulk skips the unique lock.

**Why impl-1 wins.** Its failures need a duplicate delivery or a crash at the wrong moment. Impl-2's stuck-forever outcomes come from ordinary events (an account deleted mid-run) and from the stated 40k production volume. Impl-1's tests are also more end-to-end, running a real queue worker through retries and failed(). Impl-2 is a bit simpler and uses slightly more idiomatic attributes, but correctness under the task's main focus decides it.
